chapter_theme: Songs at Kalahasti (திருக்காளத்தி): the poet sets household life and the body that ends as carrion against Siva-knowledge and the golden feet, asks the Lord to rule him without bowing to others or clinging to the world, and asks, troubled in a body of five elements, for a steady mind; the praise names Murugan the guru on Siva's shoulders and Kalahasti as the southern Kailasa.

446.reading: The poet describes himself carried along in this body with the five cheats, wearied by household life, delighting in kin, cherishing his family, until he is laid in a pit as a corpse for vultures and dogs to eat and the body-hut decays; he asks Murugan to mark him, hold him on the shore of release's unfailing bliss, dry up the false roots of the world's maya, and give him Siva-knowledge and the golden feet. The praise names Murugan the son of Siva who burned the cities to dust and burned Kama of the cane bow, who struck down Sura so the eight directions feared, who embraced the girl in hunter's guise in the holy forest, and who takes in even the lowest who come for Siva's attainment at Kalahasti.
446.nuance: The fault confessed is not lust but the ordinary householder's life (சமுசாரம், சுற்றம், குடிபேணி), followed straight into the grave pit where vultures and dogs feed. சிவஞானம் பொற்கழல் joins knowledge and the feet as one gift. The opening lines (சரக்கேறித் தப்பதி, பரிக்காயம்) and குரக்கோணம் are obscure.

447.reading: A short song: the poet asks that, so he neither bows his head to others nor aims at the attachments of worldly men, Murugan, without making him suffer, set his peerless flower feet on him and rule him. The praise names Murugan the dancer, lover of the true principle, who dwells in the minds of those who think of him and gives his holy feet to the freed, the Lord of Kalahasti.
447.nuance: சிரத்தானத்திற் பணியாதே may mean 'without my bowing my head' to men, or ask for the feet to be set on the head (சிரத்தானம்); the reading depends on the split. கர்த்தத்துவ நேசா is obscure.

448.reading: The poet speaks of the human form assembled by the five in the world of moving and unmoving things that Brahma creates, of wandering in the attachments that bind and failing to cross women's deceit, and of being troubled as disease and deeds cover the body; he asks Murugan to protect him by grace and give him a mind that does not waver. The praise names Murugan, son of the anklet-wearing beauty at Siva's left, with the cock banner, the guru who crawled on the shoulders of Siva of the crescent, serpent, bow and trident, whose throat shines with the poison of the sea; it tells of the Sarabha that flew raging to crush the pride of Vishnu as the lion, and ends at the southern Kailasa, Kalahasti, where one did penance so the sin of punishing the sun would end.
448.nuance: பஞ்சவர் கூடித் திரண்டது ஓர் நர உரு: the body is made by 'the five', the elements, gathered together. கலங்கிடா மதி, an unshaken mind, is the whole request. The Sarabha story (சிங்கமதாகத் திரிந்த மால், சிம்புள்) and the closing lines on the sun (செங்கதிரோனைக் கடிந்த தீவினை) are told obliquely, and who did penance at Kalahasti is not clear.

links.note: Both end the cherished body as carrion: the Naladiyar's vultures tear the stinking cart once its axle breaks, and 446 lays the householder in a pit for vultures and dogs. The Naladiyar's target is the praise of perfumes and garlands; 446's is family life.

The Kural says what is called virtue is household life itself (அறன் எனப்பட்டதே இல்வாழ்க்கை). The song confesses that very life, wearied in samsara, delighting in kin and cherishing the family (சமுசாரம், சுற்றத்தவரோடு இன்பத் தழைத்து, குடிபேணி), as what leads him straight to the grave pit, and asks for the roots of the world's maya to be dried. On the reading that the song counts householding itself, not its excess, as the fault, the two judge the same life oppositely.

The song asks that, not aiming at the attachments of worldly men (செகத்தோர் பற்றைக் குறியாதே), the Lord set his peerless flower feet on him and rule him (மலர்த்தாள் வைத்து எத்தனை ஆள்வாய்), with சிரத்தானம் possibly naming the head. Tirumular says the Lord set his foot on his head so that his bonds were cut (கால்கொண்டு என் சென்னியிற் கட்டறக் கட்டற) and his heart's delusion ended. Tirumular reports as done what the song asks for, and names its effect: the feet on the head end the attachment.

The song says the human form is the five gathered and massed together (பஞ்சவர் கூடித் திரண்டது ஓர் நர உரு) in the cosmos Brahma creates. Tirumular's creation verse has the five crowd together and become the five elements from which the worlds take form (ஐந்தும் செறிந்து ஐந்து பூதமாய்). The same assembling of five that builds the world builds the body the song finds frail, disease-covered and in need of an unshaken mind.
